lines.text: arose was: is then man's relationship to God the relationship
of a slave to his master? Is man wholly surrendered to the
arbitrary power of God? so here the question which we have
to face is: Is not God acting unjustly if He behaves like this
householder who gives no more pay to those workers who
for twelve long hours bore the burden of the day and the
scorching heat than to those who worked only for one hour
at sunset? Equal recompense is given to unequal work! Is
not this an act of injustice?
This impression is strengthened if we set beside the
parable of Jesus that of a Jewish scribe which outwardly
bears a complete resemblance to it. This parable speaks of a
king who had hired many workers for the completion of a
task. One of them distinguished himself by his industry and
skill, with the result that the king took him by the hand and
walked to and fro with him. At evening time the workers
came and the king gave them all the same reward. Those
who had worked the whole day long complained saying:
"We have worked all day long and this fellow has worked
for only two hours, yet he also has received full payment!"
The king made answer: "In two hours he achieved more
than you did in the whole day!" Thus in this instance too
the same reward was given for an unequal amount of work,
yet this was only so in appearance. In reality an equal
amount of work was performed. Our sense of justice is thus
satisfied. For in this case it is made clear why the shorter
time of work was rewarded equally with the longer time; in
the shorter interval as much was performed as in the longer.
Here too then the principle is observed: equal pay for equal
performance!
Now it is against this very principle that the parable of
Jesus protests. In the parable of Jesus it is a question of equal
pay for unequal work. In order to understand this we must
first of all consider what kind of a reward is in question. It is
the reward which God gives to men. In His parable Jesus is
not of course concerned to expound and teach basic social
principles as to how employees should be treated, He is
